summary: The patch only guards `_aggregate_score_dicts` against an empty score list, masking the IndexError symptom rather than fixing the root cause: the generator passed as `cv` is exhausted after the first `cross_val_score` call inside SequentialFeatureSelector's candidate loop. It prevents the crash but leaves SFS scoring most feature candidates against an empty CV, silently producing nan/arbitrary selections.

issues.description: Wrong layer of fix. Real bug is generator/iterable-of-splits exhaustion: check_cv/_CVIterableWrapper materializes the generator on the first cross_val_score call, so every later call in SFS's loop gets an empty split set. Correct fix is to materialize splits to a list once in SequentialFeatureSelector (or upstream), not to special-case empty results in the shared low-level aggregation utility.

Fix is incomplete/incorrect end-to-end. With the generator consumed, all feature candidates after the first evaluation receive an empty CV, yielding empty/nan scores. Returning `{}` stops the exception but SFS then selects features from meaningless scores — the documented 'pass an iterable of splits' behavior still does not actually work correctly.

Returning `{}` from `_aggregate_score_dicts` for empty input can propagate an empty dict into cross_validate result assembly (e.g. results['fit_time']), risking KeyError or malformed outputs on other empty-CV paths that previously failed loudly; masking the empty case in a widely-used helper changes failure semantics silently.
